Physical reasoning: Reactor temperature is governed by the jacket-side energy balance: heat generated by reaction minus heat removed by the reactor cooling-water (CW) circuit. The CW removal rate is set by the CW flow valve (xmv_10), and valve characteristics are inherently nonlinear (Cv*f(x)), so I model the cooling-driven heat-removal term as proportional to xmv_10^2 (equal-percentage/quadratic valve characteristic) rather than a bare linear term — more valve opening removes more heat, so this term should carry a NEGATIVE sign on ΔT.

The CW outlet temperature (xmeas_21) reflects the jacket's actual heat-exchange effectiveness: when the coolant exits hotter, the driving ΔT across the jacket wall shrinks, so less heat is actually removed for a given flow, causing reactor temperature to rise — a POSITIVE sign. Because this heat conducts through the metal jacket wall (a real transport delay), I lagged it by 5 samples rather than anchoring on lag1, per the guidance about thermal-wall delays being longer than one sample.

I also retain a self-damping term on xmeas_9_lag1 (negative sign, expected from any accumulation-type equation — as the reactor heats up, radiative/conductive losses and increased cooling driving force pull it back down), which is explicitly permitted even though it references the target's own history.

I deliberately avoided xmeas_1 and xmv_3 (forbidden due to CCF asymmetry) and avoided using xmeas_7/8 (reactor pressure/level) or any separator/stripper accumulation variables per the cross-unit trap rule. All variables used (xmv_10, xmeas_21, and target's own lag) are physically local to the reactor's own thermal/cooling subsystem, so this should not suffer from the cross-unit spurious correlation issue. If the sign check fails on c[1] or c[2], I will suspect valve-response confounding (xmv_10 being a controller's near-instant reaction to xmeas_9) and pivot toward a longer-lag or pure control-law framing instead of re-justifying the same law.

Given two consecutive sign-check failures on the same energy-balance/cooling-jacket law, I am switching law categories rather than re-tuning lags again.

New approach: model reactor temperature rise via reaction heat release tied to reactant inflow rate. xmeas_2 (D Feed Flow) is a genuine mass-balance measurement of reactant entering the reactor; more D feed (all else equal) drives more exothermic reaction extent and hence a temperature rise at the next step — a direct instance of the reaction-kinetics/consumption law's inflow term (expected positive sign on Δxmeas_9). I paired it only with the theoretically mandatory self-damping term on xmeas_9_lag1 (expected negative, accumulation/mean-reversion), and dropped the previously-failed cooling-loop terms entirely rather than trying to patch them with new lags. This keeps the model minimal (3 coefficients) to reduce collinearity-driven coefficient blow-up like the c[3]=127 seen previously, and avoids any cross-unit accumulation variables (xmeas_2 is a feed-flow flux crossing into the reactor boundary, not a neighboring unit's pressure/level/temperature state). If xmeas_2's sign also fails, the next step will be to test D Feed Valve (xmv_1) with an explicit nonlinear valve characteristic under law 4 instead of assuming linear flow-to-heat coupling.
